1. Validate the current bill: confirm meter reads imply 1,657 kWh (63,157 − 61,500), line items sum to $296.77 ($18.79 + $57.62 + $220.36), and the change versus last month is +$18.12 ($296.77 − $278.65); flag any arithmetic mismatch as a suspected billing error.

2. Map both billing periods to the AEP Ohio tariff by date: last month (2026-06-20 to 2026-07-20) and current (2026-07-20 to 2026-08-19) both fall entirely under the post-2026-04-10 tariff (fixed $18.788; tier-1 variable $0.0347738 + $0.13299 = $0.1677638/kWh for the first 2,000 kWh), so there is no rate change and price_usd = 0.

3. Compute days_usd: both periods are 30 days, so days_usd = 0.

4. Estimate weather_usd from NOAA degree days: compare last month (CDD 385.5 / HDD 0.5) to current (CDD 291 / HDD 0), derive a weather-to-kWh coefficient from the bill history, convert the weather-driven kWh difference to dollars at the effective variable rate ($0.1677638/kWh), or set weather_usd = 0 if no defensible coefficient can be estimated.

5. Set usage_usd as the residual so price_usd + days_usd + weather_usd + usage_usd equals exactly +$18.12; this captures household usage changes not explained by price, days, or weather.

6. Check for a billing error: model the current period with the tariff (fixed $18.788 + 1,657 kWh × $0.1677638 ≈ $296.77) and last month similarly (≈ $278.65); both match the actual totals within rounding, so billing_error_suspected = false and billing_error_usd = null.

7. Return only the JSON object with keys price_usd, days_usd, weather_usd, usage_usd, billing_error_suspected, and billing_error_usd.
